q: 1. The operation of removal of impurities or clay adhering to iron ores, is known as .....
explain: Dressing (or concentration) removes clay and other impurities adhering to the ore by washing or crushing before further treatment.

q: 2. If the iron ore contains clay as an impurity, the flux added during calcinations is .....
explain: Clay is acidic, so a basic flux such as limestone is added to combine with it and form slag.

q: 3. Pit iron made from haematite ores free from sulphur, phosphorus and copper, is known as .....
explain: Bessemer pig iron is made from pure haematite ores free from sulphur, phosphorus and copper.

q: 4. Pig iron obtained from the furnace which is properly provided with fuel at a very high temperature, is called .....
explain: With plenty of fuel and high temperature, carbon separates as graphite, giving grey (foundry) pig iron.

q: 5. If the furnace is provided with insufficient fuel at low temperatures, the type of pig iron produced, is called .....
explain: Insufficient fuel and low temperature keep carbon combined, giving white (forge) pig iron.

q: 6. The variety of pig iron used for the manufacture of steel by Bessemer process, is .....
explain: Bessemer pig iron, being low in sulphur and phosphorus, is used in the Bessemer process.

q: 7. The yield strength and tensile strength of low carbon steel may be improved by the addition of .....
explain: As per the answer key, vanadium. It refines grain and raises yield and tensile strength of low carbon steel.

q: 8. German silver is an alloy of .....
explain: German silver contains no silver; it is an alloy of copper, nickel and zinc. Options c and d are identical in the book, and the key gives c.

q: 9. Stainless steel resists corrosion due to .....
explain: Chromium forms a thin, stable oxide film on the surface that protects the steel from corrosion.

q: 10. Brass is an alloy of .....
explain: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.

q: 11. Pointing is the process whereby
options: the masonry joints are filled up with mortar after raking out for small depth
the grooves are cut on a plastered surface to give a look of masonry
small circles looking like points are cut out at random of a plastered surface
explain: Pointing involves raking out mortar joints to a small depth and refilling them with fresh mortar for a neat, weatherproof finish.

q: 12. Wrought iron contains carbon upto .....
explain: Wrought iron is almost pure iron with carbon up to about 0.15%.

q: 13. Wrought iron is manufactured from pig iron by .....
explain: Wrought iron is produced from pig iron through refining, puddling and shingling, so all are correct.

q: 14. Forge pig may be converted to wrought iron by .....
explain: Forge (white) pig iron is converted to wrought iron by puddling in a reverberatory furnace.

q: 15. Brittleness of cold is due to an excess of .....
explain: Excess phosphorus makes iron brittle when cold (cold shortness).

q: 16. Wrough iron contains carbon upto
explain: Wrought iron is a nearly pure form of iron with very low carbon content, typically up to about 0.25%.

q: 17. Red short iron cracks when bent due to the presence of .....
explain: Excess sulphur makes iron brittle at red heat (red shortness).

q: 18. The process of decarbonising the pig iron completely and then adding proper percentage of carbon for manufacturing steel is called .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: this description usually matches the Bessemer or open hearth process, so the key answer looks doubtful.

q: 19. Monel metal is an alloy of .....
explain: Monel metal is mainly nickel (about 67%) and copper (about 30%).

q: 20. The proportions of copper and zinc in Muntz metal are .....
explain: Muntz metal is 60% copper and 40% zinc.

q: 21. The base metal in Y-alloy is .....
explain: Y-alloy is an aluminium-based alloy containing copper, nickel and magnesium.

q: 22. The process of manufacturing steel by heating short lengths of wrought iron bars mixed with charcoal in the clay crucibles and collecting the molten iron into moulds, is known as .....
explain: Melting wrought iron with charcoal in clay crucibles and casting it is the crucible process.

q: 23. Bessemer process is used for the manufacture of .....
explain: The Bessemer process converts molten pig iron into steel by blowing air through it.

q: 24. Softer variety of steel may e obtained by .....
explain: As per the answer key, the Bessemer process gives a softer (low carbon, mild) steel.

q: 25. The steel which contains fissures and cavities manufactured by .....
explain: Cementation produces blister steel, whose surface shows blisters, fissures and cavities caused by escaping gases.

q: 26. Cast steel is manufactured by .....
explain: Cast steel is made by the crucible process, melting steel or wrought iron with charcoal in crucibles.

q: 27. For high grade instruments the steel preferred to, is .....
explain: Cast steel is homogeneous, hard and takes a fine edge, so it is used for high grade instruments and tools.

q: 28. The steel used in R.C.C. work is .....
explain: Mild steel is ductile and weldable, so it is used as reinforcement in R.C.C.

q: 29. Galvanizing means covering iron with a thin coat of
explain: Galvanizing is the process of coating iron or steel with a protective layer of zinc to prevent rusting.

q: 30. Vanadium steel is generally used for .....
explain: As per the answer key, vanadium steel is used for axles and springs because of its toughness and fatigue resistance.

q: 31. The type of steel used for precision leveling staff, is .....
explain: Invar has almost zero thermal expansion, so it is used for precision levelling staves and measuring tapes.

q: 32. Invar contains .....
explain: Invar is an iron-nickel alloy with about 36% nickel. The book prints 'nicked' and '30% to nickel' in options a and c.

q: 33. Galvanizing means covering iron with a thin coat of .....
explain: Galvanizing coats iron or steel with zinc to protect it from rust.

q: 34. For the manufacture of stainless steel, steel is mixed with .....
explain: As per the answer key, chromium (stainless steel also contains some nickel).

q: 35. The carbon content in wrought iron varies from
explain: Wrought iron has a very low carbon content, generally between 0.10% and 0.25%.

q: 36. The most impure form of iron, containing carbon in between 2.0 to 4.5% is known as
explain: Cast iron has the highest carbon content (2.0-4.5%), making it the most impure common form of iron.

q: 37. The properties of cast iron are
options: It can be easily forged and welded
explain: Cast iron's high carbon content and brittle grain structure make it non-magnetizable, unlike wrought iron or steel.

q: 38. Stainless steel contains .....
explain: The common 18/8 stainless steel has about 18% chromium and 8% nickel.

q: 39. Cast iron contains carbon approximately .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: cast iron is usually quoted as about 2 to 4.5% carbon, so the printed range is wide.

q: 40. Settle contains carbon approximately .....
explain: 'Settle' is a misprint for steel in the book. Steel contains about 0.05 to 1.75% carbon.

q: 41. Wrought iron contains carbon about .....
explain: Wrought iron contains about 0.15% carbon (up to 0.15%).

q: 42. Mild steel is used for .....
options: structural works in beams, joints and girders
explain: Mild steel is used in structural members such as beams, joists and girders.

q: 43. Wrought iron is used for .....
explain: Wrought iron is used for small water pipes, railings and similar items.

q: 44. The steel used for the manufacture of rails, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, Bessemer steel is used for rails.

q: 45. Cast iron is used for .....
explain: Cast iron is strong in compression, so it is used for columns and struts.

q: 46. Which material has the highest electrical conductivity?
explain: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of all metals, surpassing copper, aluminium, and steel.

q: 47. The property of steel enabling it to be drawn into thin wires is called
explain: Ductility is the physical property of a material associated with the ability to be hammered thin or stretched into wire without breaking.

q: 48. The Property of metals because of which they can be transformed into different shapes by heating is called
explain: Malleability is the ability of a metal to be deformed under compression, often improved by heating, allowing it to be rolled or hammered into sheets.

q: 49. The property due to which steel can withstand hammer blows is called
explain: Toughness is the ability of a material to absorb energy and deform plastically without fracturing, essential for resisting impact or hammer blows.

q: 50. Pig iron made from haematite are free from sulphur, phosphorus and copper is known as
explain: Bessemer pig iron is high-quality pig iron low in phosphorus and sulphur, specifically suitable for the Bessemer steel-making process.
